analysis.session_summary: BOJ policy was the anchor: the Bank of Japan hiked to <1.25% inline, but JPY slid with mean -0.514% and USD/JPY +73.8 pips; BoJ's Ueda saying it will take time to determine 2% inflation is sustainable reinforced the dovish take. GBP outperformed after Retail Sales m/m printed 0.5% vs -0.2% forecast, lifting GBP/USD +33.6 pips and pushing EUR/GBP -23.5 pips. CHF led majors (+0.32%), with USD/CHF -21.2 pips and EUR/CHF -26.4 pips, while SPX -13.5 points and VIX +0.848% show defensive tone. Oil fell with Brent/USD -0.855% despite the Saudi supply headline.

themes.theme: BOJ hike fails to support JPY; dovish Ueda fuels yen weakness
themes.evidence: BOJ Policy Rate printed <1.25% inline but JPY mean was -0.514%; USD/JPY closed +73.8 pips and Ueda said it will take time to determine if 2% inflation is sustainable.

themes.theme: Sterling outperforms on strong consumer data
themes.evidence: Retail Sales m/m actual 0.5% vs forecast -0.2%; GBP mean +0.312%, GBP/USD +33.6 pips, EUR/GBP -23.5 pips.

themes.theme: Swiss franc and defensive assets bid
themes.evidence: CHF mean +0.32%; USD/CHF -21.2 pips, EUR/CHF -26.4 pips, NZD/CHF -21.5 pips; SPX -13.5 points and VIX +0.848%.

leg_notes.EUR/USD: EUR/USD chopped around 1.14736 with legs of +15.4, -12.0, +10.4, -31.9, +16.3 pips; no single catalyst dominated, leaving net -2.5 pips near mid-range.
leg_notes.GBP/USD: GBP/USD built +24.1 pips early, gave back -37.4 pips around Lagarde, then rallied +45.8 pips into the close to end +33.6 pips in the upper part of its 50.1-pip range.
leg_notes.USD/JPY: USD/JPY's +192.5-pip overnight surge was only partly repaid with -120.7 pips late, leaving it +73.8 pips and close at 42% of its 217.2-pip range.
leg_notes.USD/CHF: USD/CHF chopped in a 34.0-pip range with a late down leg of -30.3 pips after an earlier +30.8 pips up leg, closing at the bottom of the range.
leg_notes.AUD/USD: AUD/USD rebounded +26.7 pips into Asia but faded -26.8 pips through London/NY, still closing +9.2 pips and mid-range.
leg_notes.NZD/USD: NZD/USD saw multiple alternating legs but ended -11.2 pips lower, closing at 37% of its range.
leg_notes.USD/CAD: USD/CAD's up leg of +37.4 pips dominated and left it +15.0 pips higher, closing at 64% of its range.

polarity_reads.read: Inline print but JPY still weakened 0.193%, implying the market had priced a more hawkish hike or guidance and the subsequent Ueda remarks dominated.
A beat of 0.5% vs -0.2% forecast produced a normal GBP strength impulse of 0.042%, confirming sterling upside is data-sensitive.
Muted -0.038% basket move inside the noise floor, so Lagarde added no fresh EUR direction.
Unscored; AUD strengthened 0.067% but with no forecast to benchmark, the move was tone rather than a measurable surprise.
Unscored with JPY stronger 0.204% in the 15-minute window, but no forecast; the reaction likely came from Q&A rather than a data surprise.

scenarios.thesis: BOJ failed to validate hawkish pricing and Ueda's time-to-determine comment leaves carry attractive; defensive CHF remains supported.
scenarios.invalidation: USD/JPY closes below 156.793 or JPY strength mean turns positive

pair_paths.rationale: The measured daily range is 217.2 pips; the +73.8 pips close leaves room for extension within that range.

CHF is the strongest major, and USD/CHF closed at the bottom of its 34.0-pip range.
GBP strength after Retail Sales beat supports continuation within the 50.1-pip range.

scenarios.name: Consolidation after BOJ/risk repricing
scenarios.thesis: Markets have absorbed BOJ and GBP data; with only Lagarde and Macklem ahead, major pairs are likely range-bound.
scenarios.invalidation: Break of the measured daily ranges on increased volume

USD/JPY is at 42% of its 217.2-pip range, leaving two-sided risk.
GBP/USD closed at 0.93 of its range, so upside may stall within the 50.1-pip range.

scenarios.name: JPY short squeeze / risk-off yen rebound
scenarios.thesis: If equities drop further or BOJ/Ueda commentary gets re-read as restrictive, JPY shorts unwind and USD/JPY gives back part of its +73.8 pips gain.
